canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. Across papers, the dominant framing is extended response generation: multi-sentence, multi-paragraph, or document-length text produced from a prompt, often in open-ended and context-specific settings. Many definitions emphasize coherent, detailed outputs that contain multiple factual claims, such as biographies, encyclopedic passages, or answers spanning hundreds or thousands of words, while some papers extend the framing to very long sequences above 10,000 tokens or even 100,000 tokens. Papers differ on what counts as success: most stress coherence, contextual relevance, logical flow, informativeness, or factual consistency across the full output, while one vision-language formulation treats the behavior as the length of the generated sequence before termination.

Variants. Papers use several neighboring labels and settings for this behavior. Common variants include open-ended generation, sometimes multilingual and explicitly unstructured; Wikipedia article generation, where models synthesize web-sourced information into sectioned articles; coherent multi-paragraph generation from unordered points; open-domain text generation about an entity using only internal knowledge in an encyclopedic style; and ultra-long sequence generation, framed as continuous coherent text up to 100K tokens. Other papers cast the behavior as complete-document or long-response writing, including essays, code, diaries, floorplans, and multimodal detailed image descriptions or extended free-form responses.

Space of elicitation and scores. Papers measure this behavior with six linked instruments. The most common are HelloBench and LongGenBench; papers also use LLM-as-a-judge, LLaVA-Bench-in-the-Wild, and LongFact, plus one other instrument. Across these uses, the instruments include evaluation benchmarks, a synthetic benchmark for following instructions over extended sequences, a prompt set of fact-seeking questions for multi-paragraph responses, a judge-based metric, and a multimodal benchmark for extended inference.

What it is taken as evidence of. Papers do not converge on a construct that this behavior directly evidences. The only linked construct is Length generalization, and one paper reports that it is related to long-form text generation by noting that effectiveness can diminish when input length exceeds the training length. Outside construct links, one paper claims a causal relationship from Instruction following to long-form text generation, and one paper reports that Code generation is related to it as another long-response task.

definitions.text: Producing full-length, structured Wikipedia-style articles from web-sourced information, including section organization and content synthesis.
papers: Hierarchical Memory Organization for Wikipedia Generation

definitions.text: The specific task of producing a well-structured and logically flowing text composed of multiple paragraphs from a collection of unordered points.
papers: SwarmAgentic: Towards Fully Automated Agentic System Generation via Swarm Intelligence

definitions.text: Producing lengthy, coherent, and informative responses to complex questions that require synthesis of knowledge across multiple topics or domains.
papers: From General Reward to Targeted Reward: Improving Open-ended Long-context Generation Models

definitions.text: The task of producing coherent and contextually relevant text sequences that are exceptionally long, such as exceeding 10,000 tokens.
papers: DrDiff: Dynamic Routing Diffusion with Hierarchical Attention for Breaking the Efficiency-Quality Trade-off

definitions.text: The task of generating a substantial number of output tokens from a relatively short input prompt, such as in essay writing or code synthesis.
papers: Dialogue Without Limits: Constant-Sized KV Caches for Extended Response in LLMs

definitions.text: The observable task of producing a continuous, coherent text sequence of exceptional length, such as 100,000 tokens.
papers: TokenSwift: Lossless Acceleration of Ultra Long Sequence Generation

definitions.text: The task of generating multi-paragraph, detailed textual answers in response to open-ended prompts.
papers: Long-form factuality in large language models

definitions.text: The task of generating coherent and relevant text over an extended context, often requiring the model to maintain consistency and track information over thousands of tokens.
papers: MiniCache: KV Cache Compression in Depth Dimension for Large Language Models

definitions.text: The observable behavior of producing coherent and extended text outputs such as articles or stories.
papers: Harnessing Diversity for Important Data Selection in Pretraining Large Language Models

definitions.text: A specific type of long-form generation that requires producing a response structured as a complete document.
papers: Integrative Decoding: Improving Factuality via Implicit Self-consistency

definitions.text: The observable generation of long-form, encyclopedic-style text about a given entity using only the model's internal knowledge, without external retrieval.
papers: Self-contradictory Hallucinations of Large Language Models: Evaluation, Detection and Mitigation

definitions.text: The observable behavior of a vision-language model producing an extended sequence of tokens, measured by the number of generated tokens before termination.

relationships.evidence: We introduced LongGenBench, a synthetic benchmark that evaluates long-form generation capabilities of language models by testing their ability to follow instructions over extended sequences. (Section 6)

relationships.paper: DAPE: Data-Adaptive Positional Encoding for Length Extrapolation
relationships.evidence: While transformer-based models exhibit satisfying performances in tasks of consistent length and distribution, their effectiveness tends to diminish sharply when the input length exceeds the training length, e.g., long document summarization, “needle in a haystack” search, and long text generation. (Section 1)

relationships.evidence: In contrast, long-response tasks, such as essay writing and code generation, generate a substantial number of output tokens during the decode phase, requiring sustained attention over growing sequences of self-generated tokens. (Section 1)
